name: Stalinism
summary: Stalinism is the system of rule built in the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin from the late 1920s to 1953. It combined socialism in one country, a planned state-owned economy, forced collectivization and rapid industrialization with a one-party state, a personality cult and mass repression justified by an intensifying class struggle. Its adherents present it as Marxism-Leninism.
scope: The Soviet system of 1927-1953 as set out in Stalin's own works (the 1939 Report to the 18th Party Congress, Dizzy with Success, Economic Problems of Socialism in the USSR) and described in the scholarship. It excludes Trotskyism, Maoism, Hoxhaism and post-1956 de-Stalinised Marxism-Leninism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: State socialism puts health services under state provision and planning, so a free universal system follows from its principles.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages are set by the state plan rather than by a legal minimum, so the question barely applies; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Stalin kept only limited commodity exchange for consumer goods and held that planning, not competition, directs production.

public-ownership.rationale: Industry is state property, which Stalin treats as the foundation of socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No private wealthy class is meant to survive; inferred from dispossession of exploiter classes.

unions-good.rationale: Unions exist but as party-led bodies serving the plan; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production was abolished and kulaks dispossessed; only personal property is protected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: There are no private corporations; where private activity remains it is under state control; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The state is meant to provide for workers, though work is expected of all; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is vested in the state or in collective farms as a whole, not in each enterprise's workforce.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Stalin held that a socialist state needs a strong intelligence service and punitive organs; the NKVD ran mass surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A tightly policed state is unlikely to permit it; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The state controlled speech broadly and officially condemned racial chauvinism; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The system centred on one leader and a cult of personality from 1929 to 1953.

state-harmful.rationale: Stalin argued the state must grow stronger, not wither, under capitalist encirclement.

limit-guns.rationale: The state held a monopoly on arms; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

empower-police-military.rationale: Stalin stressed a strong army, punitive organs and intelligence service; the security apparatus grew enormously.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prostitution was treated as a capitalist vestige; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

decide-locally.rationale: Power was centralised in the party and state; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

rehabilitation.rationale: Punishment was harsh, with mass executions and camps, though labour 'correction' was the official language.

traditional-family.rationale: The regime reversed Lenin-era family liberalisation, banning abortion in 1936 and re-criminalising homosexuality in 1934.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexuality was re-criminalised in 1934; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion was banned again in 1936; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

more-religion-public.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and mass persecution of religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Official doctrine condemned racism and promoted the friendship of peoples; inferred, though practice included ethnic deportations.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Women's issues were largely ignored and sex roles were reaffirmed; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Stalinism revived patriotic propaganda and Tsarist-era traditions, per Daniels.

gradual-change.rationale: Collectivization and industrialization were imposed rapidly from above.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The USSR was a closed state; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Stalin prized Soviet sovereignty and spoke of using force against aggressors; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Foreign trade was a state matter and Stalin described two rival world markets.

nation-first.rationale: Socialism in one country put the USSR's consolidation ahead of world revolution.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Intervention was justified in terms of security or class interest, not human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Borders and state are retained until capitalist encirclement ends; open borders are at best a distant aim.

limit-growth.rationale: Rapid industrial growth was the central aim; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the productionist ideology puts growth first.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Stalinism pursued industrial and technical modernisation, while distorting some sciences.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from enthusiasm for heavy industry and state power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds revolution necessary; the USSR itself came from one.

experts-over-public.rationale: Stalin praised a new Soviet intelligentsia, while the party decided; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The planned economy replaced the NEP and Stalin defended its balanced-development law.

socialized-markets.rationale: Stalin kept commodity production in consumer goods, without private capital, for a period.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is state or collective property, so a land tax is moot; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Concentration of inherited wealth is contrary to socialism; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution is by work under socialism; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Foreign trade was controlled by the state to protect planned industry; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Investment followed the plan, with priority to heavy industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Collectivization ended small peasant property; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Stalin held that commodity circulation and money would vanish once a single sector replaced two, though wages remain under socialism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state bank is part of the planned economy; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wages and prices are set by the state plan; class struggle rather than partnership is the framework.

one-party-rule.rationale: The party led a totalitarian one-party state; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The regime was a revolutionary opponent of monarchy; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

democracy-best.rationale: The regime claimed to be democratic but ran a one-man police state and treated plain voter choice as bourgeois.

direct-votes.rationale: Real decisions rested with the party leadership; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviets were formally the organs of power but in practice were party-controlled.

right-to-secede.rationale: The formal doctrine of national self-determination included secession, but it was suppressed in practice.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leadership is justified by party doctrine and training, not by nature; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Great Terror executed hundreds of thousands; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

war-builds-character.rationale: Official rhetoric stressed peace and defence, not war as virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church and state were formally separated while religion was persecuted.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Militant atheism rules this out; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Stalin insisted on a strong state army and punitive organs; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

military-superiority.rationale: Stalin warned of capitalist encirclement and said the USSR would answer blow for blow.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The USSR was a multinational state built on the friendship of nations, though some peoples were deported.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle is the core of Marxism-Leninism, and Stalin held it to intensify.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialism distributes by work; full equality comes only in communism; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land was state-controlled; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Imperialism is condemned; reparations are inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Union was organised on class and ideological lines; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collectivist ethics reject individual self-interest as a moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual rights were subordinated to the party and state; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The regime pursued the transformation of nature; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

limit-population.rationale: The state encouraged births; abortion was banned in 1936; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrialisation was the central goal; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Great Turn pushed rapid change regardless of disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred; state control of science; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; decisions rested with the party; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A strong intelligence service is held necessary; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: The regime pursued progress toward communism, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy was justified by doctrine, such as the 1938 Short Course.

direct-action.rationale: Change was meant to come through the party and state, not spontaneous direct action; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Terror and coercion were used to build socialism; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrialisation was the goal; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stalin said essential town-country and mental-manual distinctions will disappear, though some remain.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism is the stated eventual aim; socialism distributes by work.

production-for-use.rationale: Planned production for social needs is held to replace capitalist profit-seeking.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Stalin held that capitalist exploitation requires private ownership and wage labour, and denied it under socialism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Stalin described a first phase of the Soviet state as suppressing exploiting classes.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farms were the form of socialist agriculture; Stalin called the artel the main link.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Stalin held wars between capitalist countries remain inevitable while imperialism exists.

taxation-theft.rationale: State power and extraction are the basis of the system; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

harm-principle.rationale: The state controlled culture, speech and private life; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The collective and the party come before individual rights; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

conscription.rationale: A large standing army is held essential; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The regime restricted emigration and rejected exit as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a class and party instrument, not a firm; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material guarantees under the plan are stressed over negative liberty.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and universities were state-controlled instruments of the party.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Soviet doctrine was environmentalist, to the point of Lysenkoism.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation ran through the party and soviets; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

total-state.rationale: The state directed the economy, education and culture, including socialist realism.

national-rebirth.rationale: The aim was socialist construction, not national decadence and rebirth; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Soviet control extended over satellite states from 1944 to 1953.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on party and state, though loyalty to Stalin was demanded.

bound-labor.rationale: Stalin condemns extra-economic coercion as a feudal feature.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is understood as class-based; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: Party doctrine claims to know the common interest; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The USSR backed Israel in 1948 but turned hostile to Zionism and 'cosmopolitans' soon after.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the closed-border, nationalities policy; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Russification and Russian as de facto state language; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Enterprises were run through the plan and party; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state controlled education; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The question belongs to market economies; the planned economy has no such debate.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom is regarded as capitalist and replaced by planning.

rule-by-example.rationale: The system rested on law, terror and an elaborate cult; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

national-self-determination.rationale: The formal nationalities doctrine upheld it, though it was overridden in practice.

force-without-un.rationale: Stalin said the USSR would respond with force to aggression; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dialectical materialism and atheism put scientific reason against religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the closed, state-centred system; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Distribution by work is the rule under socialism; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rests on class struggle; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The regime used classical heritage and the Short Course; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Stalin described two hostile world camps and markets; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Socialism in one country gave national framing, though internationalism was professed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Formal law gave equality, though policy was pronatalist; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Private moneylending was incompatible with the planned economy; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Official doctrine proclaimed equality of races and friendship of nations.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Stalin described the state as an instrument to suppress exploiters and defend against encirclement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from industrialisation drive; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from nationalities policy; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiratorial claim alien to Marxism-Leninism; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections were single-list; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

national-mission.rationale: Stalin dismissed the export of revolution as nonsense; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Women's issues were largely ignored; class is the key analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Official doctrine treated bureaucrats as 'wreckers' to be purged, not the ruling party; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics was rejected in Soviet doctrine; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The NKVD operated as the state's instrument of terror; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A strong, directing state is central; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Official doctrine proclaimed friendship of nations and rejected racism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formal equality was proclaimed, though class enemies and ethnic groups were persecuted.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalin introduced the doctrine that socialism could be built in the USSR alone.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Marxism-Leninism condemns colonialism and imperialism; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Soviet law was uniform and secular; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious propaganda was restricted; inferred; Stalinist sources give no stated position on this, so it is left neutral.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No religious basis; collectivization led to mass livestock slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and enforced it in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin said the state will remain and be strengthened while capitalist encirclement lasts, and rebuked those who asked why it was not withering away.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stalinism rested the party-state own right to rule on its vanguard role and the working class historic interest, not on the freely expressed agreement of the ruled, and it suppressed dissent.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Stalinist doctrine treated science and culture as class-bound ('bourgeois' versus 'proletarian'), inferred from this Marxist-Leninist framing; Stalin also denied that language was class superstructure.

trade-surplus.rationale: The Soviet state monopolised foreign trade to import machinery and pursue self-sufficiency under encirclement; no stated doctrine on surpluses, so inferred and split.

population-transfer.rationale: Stalin's government deported whole nationalities it deemed disloyal, such as Chechens, Crimean Tatars and Volga Germans, as a security measure.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Stalinism justified forced collectivization and mass repression by the goal of socialism and an intensifying class struggle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Soviet doctrine credited planning and collective ownership, and promoted 'socialist emulation' rather than market rivalry; inferred from that economic model.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The one-party state suppressed all rival parties as agents of hostile classes and powers.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stalinism defined freedom through material security and the socialist state, and tolerated arbitrary party power; inferred, as the republican concept was not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet rule fused power in the party-state and rejected checks and balances as bourgeois forms.

vanguard-party.rationale: Stalinism inherited Lenin's doctrine of a disciplined vanguard party leading the working class and the state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The state claimed to rule for workers and peasants, but its policy priority was industrialization and state power; inferred from its class rhetoric.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing and land were state or collective property and the doctrine limited personal property to consumer goods, so a right to buy state homes fits poorly; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were effectively unlawful because unions were party-led bodies serving the plan; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxism-Leninism locates poverty in property relations and class rule, not in numbers of people, so the regime rejected the Malthusian view.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy officially preached internationalism and condemned national chauvinism, though it also deported peoples; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Office was filled by party appointment of cadres, and the regime treated plain voter choice as bourgeois; chance selection has no place.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Stalin argued that class struggle intensifies as socialism advances, and the regime justified mass repression and extrajudicial courts on that basis.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Prices and distribution were fixed by the state plan, and the state set prices under socialism.

party-controls-media.rationale: The press, radio and publishing were state and party controlled, with censorship to guide opinion.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stalin called for strengthening the army under party leadership, and political commissars made the army answer to the party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The USSR was a closed state that guarded entry and citizenship under encirclement; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Party maximum and the egalitarian rhetoric of Marxism-Leninism favoured modest official pay, though Stalin's regime in practice gave the elite large privileges and Stalin attacked wage equalisation; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism, with free debate then binding obedience, was the party rule Stalinism inherited and enforced to the extreme.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Stalin stressed the sovereign Soviet state under capitalist encirclement, and the regime treated the EU-style pooling of power as a capitalist arrangement; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive power was concentrated in Stalin and the party leadership, though formally the legislature was a rubber stamp; the statement's form is only loosely matched, so inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The regime persecuted the church, then in 1943 restored the bishop-led Moscow Patriarchate under state control; adherents had no view on church governance as such.

clerical-rule.rationale: The regime practised militant atheism and persecuted clergy, so clerical authority over the state was unthinkable.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's revolutionary defeatism targeted capitalist powers, while Stalin demanded defence of the Soviet fatherland; adherents would apply it to others' wars, not their own.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Socialist realism and state censorship shaped art to build the new Soviet person, as the Stalinist cultural system documents.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Stalin held office as General Secretary without term limits until death, and the one-party system had no limits on leaders; inferred for presidents.

recall-officials.rationale: The Soviet constitutions nominally allowed recall of deputies, but the one-party system left it unused, and adherents held that the party, not voters, removed officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of socialism in one country and wary self-reliance toward capitalist powers; Stalin's postwar system however built alliances in the Soviet bloc.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing was state-owned and allocated under the planned economy rather than distributed as family-owned homes; no stated position on private ownership of homes.

people-in-arms.rationale: Stalinism built a large professional, party-controlled Red Army and treated military power as a state monopoly; inferred, not a stated position.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Stalin's works aim at removing the contrast between town and country and the programme was rapid urban industrialization; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: reunification was not a defined Stalinist principle and Soviet border policy was pragmatic.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Stalinism promoted a new Soviet intelligentsia and technical education, though intellectuals were also purged.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Soviet doctrine proclaimed equality of nations, yet Stalinism also ranked Russia first and class stages as higher; split, inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Stalinist rule used capital punishment extensively against alleged enemies of the state, as documented in the scholarship.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Stalin-era return to traditional family policy, including the 1936 abortion ban.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Stalinism presented itself as Marxism-Leninism, a materialist and atheist doctrine that rejected religious accounts of origins.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the state's control of culture and censorship under Stalinism, which restricted erotic material.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet approach to citizenship as tied to the state and class loyalty rather than ethnic descent; no stated position.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet nationalities policy of promoting national-language schools in the 1920s-30s, though it was later curtailed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from the Stalinist state's campaigns against religion, which allowed no exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the Stalinist demand for conformity and state control of personal life, art and thought.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Stalin's anti-imperialist line treats capitalist powers as exploiters of weaker countries, so writing off debts to them is inferred; no source addresses debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Stalin held that national freedom was tied to the socialist transformation of society; inferred from the 1939 report's account of the state and capitalist encirclement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The system rested on one-party rule and constitutions issued from the party leadership rather than freely elected assemblies; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid industrialization and forced collectivization were pursued under a one-party state that suppressed dissent in the name of building socialism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Stalin's writings frame foreign relations as a contest with capitalist encirclement rather than a universal duty of the rich to the poor; adherents are not clearly for or against.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Soviet security policy stressed self-reliance against capitalist encirclement, so an independent deterrent fits; nuclear weapons themselves are not discussed in the sources, so this is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Soviet head of state was chosen by the legislature under one-party control rather than by direct popular vote; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: All credit and finance were subordinated to the state plan, leaving no room for a bank independent of the government; inferred from the planning system.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Stalinism's sources do not address trading territory for peace and its record mixes annexation with diplomacy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Under Stalin's two property sectors, productive property is state or collective and subordinate to the plan, with personal property allowed; read as a common-good view, inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Stalin declared socialism built in the USSR and held that the state-owned planned economy was socialist, with exploitation abolished.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Stalinism put rapid industrial growth first, so restricting projects over uncertain risk cuts against it; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report favours mutual assistance pacts against aggressors, though Soviet practice was opportunistic; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The USSR annexed the Baltic states and eastern Poland in 1939-40 and treated them as legitimately incorporated; inferred from that practice.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Stalinism brought militant atheism and the persecution of religion, with church property taken and clergy placed under state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Party leader, identified with the state, was a partisan figure; the one-party state has no non-partisan head.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 17 nominally allowed secession, but the regime crushed nationalist movements and deported peoples; practice favoured keeping territory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The republics were formally autonomous but all shared one socialist legal and economic system under Party direction.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Militant atheism rules out a sacred ruler; Stalin's cult was secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive tax on higher incomes fits socialist redistribution; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions form people, and the regime aimed to remake them, as in the 'new Soviet man'; Lysenkoism echoed this in biology.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Formally the state claimed socialist legality, but in practice Stalin and the Party stood above the law; adherents would not endorse the claim in doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Soviet space work was not a Stalin-era doctrinal goal and the question barely applies.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule is held to belong wholly to the working class through the Party's dictatorship of the proletariat, not a mix of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: From 1929 Stalin's image spread through statues, posters and banners and he was identified with the state.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family policy in this era (1944 law) favoured the state's interest in births and left fathers with few duties; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Stalin held that class struggle sharpens as socialism advances and justified purges by hidden enemies, including within the party.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land went to peasants in 1917, but Stalinism then collectivised it; only partly matches the statement, so inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The Stalinist state deported entire nationalities and did not honour return rights; inferred from practice.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Soviet expansion in 1939-40 used kin-people arguments in part but was framed by security and socialism; adherents give no clear doctrine.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1936 Constitution separates church and state and equal rights for all; Stalinist practice persecuted religion but did not legislate against apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Stalinism was militantly secular and opposed religious dress and customs, so compelled covering is rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Stalin kept national currencies and a closed monetary system under the plan; a shared currency is inferred as not a goal.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The USSR was built on a socialist union, not ethnic or kin unification across borders; Pan-Slavism was dismissed. Inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Soviet doctrine held nations should be national in form and socialist in content, run by a unified state; separate self-governing minority institutions are inferred as rejected.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Stalinist doctrine opposed Zionism and stressed assimilation within the Soviet state; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stalin held that economic laws and the mode of production determine social change, as in Marxist historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Stalinist economy is state-owned and planned, with concentration of production as policy; competition-based antitrust is inferred as rejected.

no-bailouts.rationale: State enterprises are propped up by the plan and not left to fail, so a ban on rescue is inferred as rejected.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: In the Stalinist state, courts and institutions answered to the party, so that majority and party will were not constrained; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights of women but set no representation quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Stalin held that the USSR must build socialism in one country amid capitalist encirclement, favouring economic independence.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Stalinism sought independence from capitalist markets, not binding standards imposed by trade deals; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Stalin held that socialism pays according to work, rejecting egalitarian levelling; moral incentives alone were not the doctrine, though used alongside.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Stalin favoured socialism in one country and rejected exporting revolution by small armed groups.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1936 Constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of origin and ended titles of the old order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Stalin-era socialism in one country was joined to Soviet patriotism and a nation-centred account of history; inferred from the overview, not from a specific source.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Stalinism condemned imperialism and colonial rule and the 1936 constitution proclaimed equal rights and a right of secession, so tutelage is rejected; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Soviet patriotism is a listed element of Stalinism, and schooling under Stalin was used to build loyalty to the Soviet state and its symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Korenizatsiia gave national preferences in the 1920s but was curtailed under Stalin, and the 1936 constitution proclaimed equal rights; Stalin's own works do not address it.

public-money-creation.rationale: A planned, state-owned economy leaves credit and money under state control; Stalin's works do not discuss money creation directly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Stalin held that capitalism is torn by contradictions, imperialist wars and a general crisis that make its eventual collapse inevitable.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Soviet policy sought lasting influence over neighbouring lands the Russian Empire had held, notably in Eastern Europe after 1945; inferred from Soviet practice.

delink-world-market.rationale: Stalin argued in 1952 that the world market had split into parallel socialist and capitalist markets and championed economic independence from the capitalist world; applied to poor countries by inference.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Stalin regarded the US working class as 'bourgeoisified' and played down advanced-country workers against Trotsky; the Wikipedia passage is itself marked citation needed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 1936 constitution guaranteed equal rights regardless of nationality or race, and private enterprise was abolished, so private discrimination has no place.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1936 constitution listed rights but they were subordinate to the party and the plan, and it was amendable by the Supreme Soviet; limiting the state by entrenched rights runs against Stalinist theory.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Soviet policy treated border questions by its own interests (1939 pact, post-war frontiers); no clear stated principle, inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Soviet state rested on a one-party hierarchy, and heads of state were chosen by the party, not contested elections; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism subordinates minorities to the majority line, and dissent was repressed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The party-state treated resistance to the leadership as treason and counterrevolution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supreme Soviet was nominally the supreme body under the 1936 constitution but the party actually ruled; ambiguous.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Soviet life accepted animal welfare in principle; sources do not address it, so inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A utilitarian, productivist view accepts using animals for food and research; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity by the privileged is a class-society idea; socialism replaces it with state provision; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Citizens were expected to take part in building socialism and the Party; withdrawal was condemned.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist theory fits the claim but Stalinist culture used mass media to mobilise its own order; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxism-Leninism accepts that bourgeois rule works partly through ideology and culture, in addition to force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Stalin's account of imperialism holds that capitalist states exploit colonies and weaker countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Soviet Union formally promoted equality among nationalities; reserving offices by birth is contrary to its stated line, though inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: Stalinism demanded the Comintern follow Moscow's direction; foreign parties were subordinated to the CPSU.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Socialism in one country: the USSR built industry on its own resources and under capitalist encirclement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Soviet territorial policy recovered lands lost to Tsarist Russia in 1939-45, but no general principle is stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Soviet policy was class-based and promoted all nationalities as equal; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Antifascism was central to Stalinist legitimacy, especially after 1941, and to Soviet foreign policy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Stalinism treated fascism as the open terrorist dictatorship of finance capital and communism as its opposite.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Soviet historiography held that the Civil War was fought over slavery and the Southern slaveholders' rebellion; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Soviet practice destroyed monuments of the old regime; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Soviet ideology held that sex equality is achieved by socialism and had no men's programmes; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Soviet ideology treated domestic violence as a vestige of the old order, not as gendered symmetry; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims universal validity and had no pluralism of political forms; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party controls the army, which is subordinate to it, with political commissars; the army may not act independently.

paid-care-work.rationale: Stalinism socialised domestic labour through services but did not endorse paying household work; mixed and inferred.

missingStatements.text: A socialist state should grow stronger, not wither away, for as long as it is surrounded by hostile states.
missingStatements.rationale: Stalin argued explicitly that the state persists and strengthens under capitalist encirclement and criticised Party members who asked why it was not dying out.

notes: Stalinism is contested as a category: its adherents regard it as simply Marxism-Leninism, and historians disagree over its continuity with Lenin. Practice (terror, deportations) often diverged from the formal doctrine, so answers on equality and self-determination are low confidence.
